Level 2 · Intermediate · Week 8

Testing: Prove It Works

A test is a tiny program that checks your program, so bugs get caught before players find them.

What you will learn

  • How to write a test with assert.
  • How to run your tests with pytest and read PASSED and FAILED.
  • How to choose normal and edge test cases that catch sneaky bugs.
  • How to use failing tests as a map to find and fix bugs.

The big idea: let the computer check your code

Checking a game by hand is slow: run it, play, look at the score… again and again. A test is a tiny function that checks another function for you, in less than a second. It uses the word assert, which means “I am sure this is true”.

A test for clamp(), which keeps a number between two limits

from clamp_tools import clamp

def test_too_big_comes_down_to_high():
    assert clamp(99, 0, 10) == 10, "99 is too big, so it should become 10"

A test has three parts: call the function with values you choose, say what you expect with ==, and add a message for when it goes wrong. The function’s name must start with test_, so that pytest can find it.

Running your tests

  • Easy way: open your test file and press Run. The bottom of the file starts pytest for you.

  • Programmer way: Tools > Open system shell…, type python -m pytest starter.py -v and press Return (if it says “command not found”, use python3).

starter.py::test_middle_value_stays_the_same PASSED     [ 50%]
starter.py::test_too_small_goes_up_to_low FAILED        [100%]
E       AssertionError: -3 is too small, so it should become 0
E       assert 0 == 5
E        +  where 0 = clamp(-3, 0, 10)
============ 1 failed, 1 passed in 0.03s ============

Read it from the bottom up. The last line is the score. The E lines say what went wrong: clamp gave back 0 but the test expected 5. When a test fails, ask: is the code wrong, or is my expected answer wrong?

Normal and edge cases

A normal case is what usually happens. An edge case is a strange corner: that is where bugs love to hide.

Function Normal case Edge cases
clamp(value, 0, 10) clamp(5, 0, 10) gives 5 too small, too big, exactly 0, exactly 10
best_score(scores) best in the middle empty list, one score, best is first, best is last
encode(msg, shift) "abc" with shift 1 letters near z, spaces and !, shift 0

TipWhy testing matters

In 1999 a spacecraft was lost on its way to Mars because two parts of its software used different units, and no test checked them together. People can only trust apps and games that have been tested. Testing your game is a way of being fair to your players.

Reflect

Think of a game you like. Write one edge case its programmers should test.

When a test fails, what two things could be wrong?

Which was harder: writing tests or fixing bugs? Why?

New words

test
A small function that checks another function and says PASSED or FAILED.
assert
“I am sure this is true.” If it is false, Python stops with AssertionError .
pytest
A helper that finds every function called test_… , runs it and reports the results.
normal case
An everyday input, like a list of three scores.
edge case
A strange corner: empty, zero, the first, the last, exactly on a limit.
expected vs actual
What the test says should happen, and what really happened.

  1. Read cipher_tools.py. Then open starter.py (your test file) and press Run.

  3. TODO 2: test a message with a space and a ! in it. My message and its secret version:

  4. TODO 3: one more test of your own (ideas: shift 0, or an empty message "").

ChallengeSpot the edge

For each function, write one normal case and one edge case (no computer needed).

Function Normal case Edge case
count_vowels(word): counts a, e, i, o, u
lives_left(lives, hits): never below 0
last_item(items): the last item

CreativeTest something of yours

Pick a function you wrote in an earlier week (for example from your Monster Stats, Word Guess or Idea Notebook). In the same folder, make a new file called my_tests.py. Import your function (from starter import my_function), write two tests (one normal, one edge), and copy the last three lines of this week’s starter.py to the bottom so that Run starts pytest. This is exactly how your final project’s tests will work. Or: draw a comic strip of a “crash-test dummy” testing a game’s strangest corner.
